name: Codeine
description: Codeine facts: uses, why it is risky in children and ultra-rapid metabolizers, schedules II to V, interactions, overdose, withdrawal, and legal access.
quick: Codeine is a mild opioid used for pain and, in some products, for cough. The body converts it into morphine, and how fast that happens varies with genetics, which makes codeine dangerous for some people. Plain codeine is Schedule II, combinations with acetaminophen are Schedule III, and low-dose cough syrups are Schedule V.
facts: Tylenol with Codeine (No. 3, No. 4); cough products
Schedule II alone; III with acetaminophen; V in low-dose cough syrups
Mild to moderately severe pain; cough (combination products, adults only)
Tablets; tablets with acetaminophen; oral solution; cough syrups

blocks.p: Codeine is approved for mild to moderately severe pain when non-opioid treatments are not enough, and in combination products to suppress cough in adults.[[1]]

Codeine itself has little effect. The liver enzyme CYP2D6 converts about 5 to 10% of it into morphine. People who are "ultra-rapid metabolizers" convert it fast and can reach dangerous morphine levels from normal doses, while "poor metabolizers" get little pain relief. The share of ultra-rapid metabolizers varies widely by ancestry.

The figures below come from the FDA-approved label and describe how prescribers typically use codeine. They are not personal dosing advice. A prescriber sets the dose for each person and adjusts it over time.[[1]]

sections.q: What are the risks and side effects of codeine?

boxed.title: FDA boxed warnings
items: Codeine exposes users to risks of addiction, misuse, and abuse, which can lead to overdose and death.
Life-threatening slowed breathing can occur, especially when starting treatment or after a dose increase.
Accidental ingestion, especially by children, can cause a fatal overdose.
Use with benzodiazepines or other central nervous system depressants, including alcohol, can cause profound sedation, slowed breathing, coma, and death.
Prolonged use during pregnancy can cause neonatal opioid withdrawal syndrome, which may be life-threatening if not recognized and treated.
Ultra-rapid metabolism of codeine has caused life-threatening breathing problems and deaths in children.
Codeine is contraindicated in children under 12, and in anyone under 18 after removal of tonsils or adenoids.[[2]]

blocks.p: **Common side effects** include constipation, drowsiness, nausea, lightheadedness, and sweating.[[1]]
**Breastfeeding:** the FDA advises against codeine while breastfeeding because babies of ultra-rapid metabolizers have been harmed by morphine in breast milk.[[2]]

sections.q: What does codeine overdose look like?

blocks.p: Codeine overdose causes pinpoint pupils, extreme drowsiness, confusion, and slow or stopped breathing. Ultra-rapid metabolizers, especially children, can overdose on ordinary doses.[[2]][[3]]

emergency.title: If someone may have overdosed
items: Call 911 if the person is unresponsive, cannot be woken, has blue or gray lips, or is breathing slowly or not at all.
Give naloxone (Narcan or a generic nasal spray, sold without a prescription) into one nostril. If there is no response after 2 to 3 minutes, give another dose.
If you are trained, give rescue breaths. Otherwise place the person on their side so they do not choke.
Stay with them. Naloxone can wear off before codeine does, so the overdose can return even after the person wakes up.
Most states have Good Samaritan laws that protect people who call 911 for an overdose from some drug charges.

sections.q: What is codeine withdrawal like, and how long does it last?

blocks.p: People who take codeine regularly for more than a few weeks become physically dependent, even when they take it exactly as prescribed. Dependence is not the same as addiction, but it means stopping suddenly causes withdrawal.[[1]]

timeline.title: Early symptoms
timeline.text: Anxiety, restlessness, yawning, sweating, runny nose, watery eyes, and muscle aches.

timeline.title: Peak withdrawal
timeline.text: Diarrhea, stomach cramps, nausea and vomiting, goosebumps, dilated pupils, fast heartbeat, and strong cravings. Rarely dangerous in healthy adults, but dehydration can be serious.

timeline.title: Lingering symptoms
timeline.text: Poor sleep, low mood, low energy, and cravings can continue for weeks. Tolerance falls quickly, which raises the risk of overdose if use restarts.

blocks.warn: After a break, the body loses tolerance within days. Returning to a previous dose of codeine can cause a fatal overdose.

blocks.p: The FDA warns against stopping opioids abruptly in people who are physically dependent. A prescriber can taper the dose gradually, often by 10% or less per month for long-term users, and medicines such as clonidine or lofexidine can ease symptoms. For opioid use disorder, buprenorphine and methadone cut the risk of death roughly in half.[[4]]

sections.q: How do you get codeine legally in the US?

blocks.p: In the United States, codeine is a Schedule III controlled substance. The only legal way to get it is with a prescription from a clinician registered with the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA), filled by a licensed pharmacy. Depending on state law, that can be a physician, nurse practitioner, or physician assistant.[[5]]

ul: **Refills:** a Schedule III prescription can be refilled up to five times within six months of the date it was written. After that, a new prescription is needed.[[6]]

**Telehealth:** federal flexibilities let DEA-registered clinicians prescribe Schedule II to V medicines after a telemedicine visit, without a prior in-person exam, through December 31, 2026. A permanent DEA rule was under final review in late 2026. State rules can be stricter.[[7]]
**Monitoring:** prescribers and pharmacists in most states check a prescription drug monitoring program, a database of controlled-substance prescriptions, before prescribing or dispensing.

**Pharmacies:** a legitimate pharmacy always requires a valid prescription, has a licensed pharmacist available, and is licensed in the state it ships to. The FDA's BeSafeRx tool and the NABP's safe pharmacy list help confirm a pharmacy is real.[[8]][[9]]
**Cost:** acetaminophen with codeine is inexpensive and widely covered.

**Schedules:** plain codeine is Schedule II. Most prescriptions are acetaminophen with codeine, which is Schedule III. Cough syrups with small amounts of codeine are Schedule V; a few states allow some to be sold by a pharmacist without a prescription, with ID and quantity limits.[[5]]

blocks.p: **Traveling:** keep the medicine in its original pharmacy container and carry a copy of the prescription. Check the rules of the destination country before travel, because many countries restrict controlled medicines or require a permit.

Yes, but only with a valid prescription and only from a pharmacy licensed in your state. Many licensed pharmacies, including mail-order pharmacies run by insurers, fill codeine prescriptions online and ship them. Buying codeine from a website that does not require a prescription is illegal, and the product is often fake.[[8]][[10]]

Prescriptions for controlled medicines are usually sent electronically, straight from the prescriber to the pharmacy you choose.
The pharmacy checks and fills it
A pharmacist verifies the prescription and your identity, then dispenses the medicine in person or by mail.

blocks.p: **Signs that an online seller is illegal:**

ul: It sells codeine with no prescription, or after only a short online questionnaire.
It takes orders through social media, messaging apps, or email.
It asks for payment in cryptocurrency, gift cards, or money transfers.
It has no US street address, no state pharmacy license, and no pharmacist to speak to.
Its prices are far below those of ordinary pharmacies, or it ships from another country.

blocks.p: The FDA's BeSafeRx tool links to each state's license lookup, and the National Association of Boards of Pharmacy lists verified online pharmacies.[[8]][[9]]

faq: No. It is contraindicated in children under 12, and in anyone under 18 after tonsil or adenoid surgery, because some children turn codeine into morphine very quickly.
Why does codeine not work for some people?
About 5 to 10% of people of European ancestry are poor CYP2D6 metabolizers and convert little codeine into morphine, so they get little pain relief.
Is codeine cough syrup legal without a prescription?
Federally, low-dose codeine cough syrups are Schedule V. A few states let pharmacists sell them without a prescription, with ID and limits; most require a prescription.
A street name for codeine-promethazine cough syrup mixed with soft drinks. The combination causes heavy sedation and has caused fatal overdoses, especially with alcohol.
How long does codeine stay in your system?
Its half-life is about 3 hours. Urine tests usually detect it for 1 to 2 days.
